It defines ARMS = ("codeword","public","explicit"), which is three arms. Its receive() at line 141 resumes the receiver checkpoint and writes the ledger plus a public digest at line 187. D, dogwhistle/honest.py, is the closest runner but has only two arms (codeword, public). It has the same receive() and digest pattern at lines 125 and 171, so it is useful for comparison. study.py (A) has two conditions, covert and no_signal. heldout.py (B) has a receiver and checkpoint flow, but I found no three-arm definition in it. Suggested 60 minutes: visibility.py 35, honest.py 10, heldout.py 8, study.py 7. I did not run any code or tests. Which files to prioritize comes from grep results only.
